newsitem.title: UK: Gold and oil tumble, copper recovers losses.
newsitem.headline: Gold and oil tumble, copper recovers losses.

text.p: Gold plunged to a new 2-1/2 year low under heavy selling while a late rally in copper on Monday dragged other base metals from their lows.
However, the base metals failed to reach last week's peaks.
IPE Brent crude oil futures prices fell sharply on news that Bagdad has agreed to all conditions for the oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
Gold closed at its lowest level since March 1995 at $375.05 per ounce, down from Friday's $376.55 finish and near to the psychological $375 barrier.
"We are at new lows for the year and if it goes beyond $375, it could get very ugly," one dealer said.
Gold has been under pressure from institutional and producer selling for several days, and several traders said they were betting on it to fall to $370.
Other precious metals were quiet with prices slightly down or almost unchanged.
The European copper market is still tight with London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks depleted, consumption picking up and scrap material being withheld.
Benchmark three months delivery copper finished at $2,204 after a late rally from a low of $2,157, versus Friday's LME kerb close of $2,187.
Traders expect scrap metals, a source of copper, would be more available following November's sharp rise in copper prices.
Also aiding the recovery was borrowing of nearby spreads, against the backdrop of a lack of available metal.
This saw copper's cash to three months backwardation at $170 from earlier levels of $145.
Copper stocks held in official LME warehouses stand at 6-1/4 year lows of 93,900 tonnes but are expected to start rising over the coming months, a move that could dent recent upside sentiment.
But traders said they expected the market to broadly consolidate ahead of Tuesday's LME stocks release.
"The market was looking overbought but is unlikely to make a serious move until the stocks are out of the way," one trader commented.
Othe metals moved in line with copper.
Aluminium edged away from support at $1,500 to settle at 1,513, versus Friday's 1,504.50.
Benchmark Northsea Brent oil shed earlier gains and moved rapidly to the red to trade 23 cents down at $22.80 a barrel by the late afternoon.
Oil prices rallied on Friday to wipe out midweek losses as much of the United States remained in the icy grip of an early winter, prompting fears of heating oil shortages.
Iraqi U.N. ambassador Nazir Hamdoon said on Monday Bagdad has agreed to all U.N. conditions that had held up the implementation of the deal.
"The market is bound to fall on this type of news, but it is still focused on winter heating oil demand," said Alistair Harris of brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London.
In soft commodities, most coffee positions maintain pre-midday losses despite slight New York gains. Benchmark January future was $3 off at $1,422.
World consumer coffee stocks rose to 9.10 million 60-kg bags at the end of September from 8.83 million in June but down from 10.94 million a year ago, UK research firm LMC International Ltd said.
Cocoa was mixed as New York trade held above support.
Bemchmark March prices were steady at 927 after earlier losses.
White sugar futures drifted lower in a sluggish start to the week's trading but the structure of the forward months remained muddled.

CBOT wheat futures traded strongly higher on follow-through buying and on expectations that the conflict between the U.S. and Turkey over shipments of U.S. wheat may be close to an end. Some key commodity prices at 1730 GMT on Monday
